area: extensions and sandbox: core/sandbox, user extension store and wiring, agent factory extension paths, skills, catalog
purpose: Let the human install declared extensions (tools, sections, hooks, wraps, triggers) that run in a QuickJS VM inside AgentDO, behind a review step, with egress and secret limits, plus a reviewed catalog and read-on-demand skills.
summary: The install gate, secret handling, egress, and effect checks are sound: only the human's socket installs, secrets go only to declared hosts, and extension requests do not follow redirects. The gaps are in what the review and check say: read tools can write yuki.state although the review says they only read, and the trigger check accepts six runs an hour while its message says at most once. Skills, the catalog, and extensions are separate; only instruction text overlaps between skills and extension sections. No high-severity problem found.

subareas.name: VM and bridge
subareas.why: The bridge is the only I/O, gated by effect (compile.ts:162, 172-173) and the calls and egress lists. Limits hold (vm.ts:4-7). Gaps: prelude helpers are visible to scripts (vm.ts:17-57), read tools may write state (compile.ts:155), and a VM can be disposed under an in-flight call (compile.ts:79-85).

subareas.name: Manifest and checker
subareas.why: checkManifest is strict (manifest.ts:111-263). The trigger rule is wrong (manifest.ts:240). check.ts runs a mock bridge (check.ts:74-111) instead of the real one, so the two can drift.

subareas.name: Extension store and install gate
subareas.why: install, uninstall, secret, and enable are reached only from the human's socket frame (user-do.ts:809-810). The agent path is propose-only (extensions.ts:194). Secrets are sealed with AAD (extensions.ts:317), filled only for declared hosts (430), and scrubbed from responses (450-454). A trigger failure after install can leave the row installed with no installed event sent (extensions.ts:265).

subareas.name: Agent wiring
subareas.why: sync() compiles changed bundles, swaps registry parts, and retains live VMs. State scope is composed per room and per agent (agent-do.ts:558-561), which is correct. retain() can dispose a VM an in-flight call still uses (factory.ts:153).

subareas.name: Skills
subareas.why: Simple and tested: strict name and folder match, escaped XML list (registry.ts:39), room skills override built-ins (registry.ts:35). read_skill re-reads every room skill on each call (skills.ts:56, 24-39).

subareas.name: Catalog
subareas.why: Generated bundles, a freshness test (user-extensions.test.ts:223-226), and every entry must pass extension_check (228-238). Doc drift only: AGENTS.md and architecture.md name scripts/gen-catalog.ts, but the file is apps/server/scripts/gen-catalog.ts.

strengths: Install gate: install, uninstall, and secret ops run only from the human's socket frame (user-do.ts:809-810). Agents and the catalog only propose (extensions.ts:194, 226).
Effects enforced at runtime for fetch and call (compile.ts:162, 172-173) with one rank table (compile.ts:41-51).
Egress checked at check time (manifest.ts:123-130) and at runtime (extensions.ts:403-405).

Secrets sealed with AAD per extension and name (extensions.ts:317, 471), sent only to declared hosts (430), cannot change the host (438), extension requests do not follow redirects (safe-fetch.ts:106-108), and responses are scrubbed (450-454).
VM isolation: loader limited to bundle files (vm.ts:115-121), escape test (script-vm.test.ts:72-79), step, memory, and wall limits.
Users never cross: the store is keyed from the UserDO's own object name (user-do.ts:116-117).

problems.title: Read tools can write yuki.state, which the review says they cannot
problems.evidence: compile.ts:155 sends every state op to stateOp with readOnly=false and no effect check. manifest.ts:293 tells the human a read tool 'only reads'. check.ts:81-88 allows writes too. No test covers it.
problems.fix: Refuse state.set and state.delete when the tool's effect is read, add a test, and mirror it in the mock. Or change the review text to 'keeps its own notes'.

problems.title: Trigger rule accepts six runs an hour; extension_check passes what install refuses
problems.evidence: manifest.ts:240 rejects only FREQ=MINUTELY but says 'at most once an hour'. Probe: checkManifest accepts FREQ=HOURLY;BYMINUTE=0,10,20,30,40,50. The real 30-minute rule is reminders.ts:16 and 621, applied only at create time (extensions.ts:284-289), and the error lands on the extension row only.
problems.fix: Pass the repeat check into checkBundle as an option, so extension_check runs the same rule as install. Fix the message.

problems.title: Prelude helpers are visible to scripts, a second name for the bridge
problems.evidence: vm.ts:17-21 declares host, hostSync, ask, makeYuki, pick, and parse as top-level const. Probe: a module sees all six as 'function'. script-vm.test.ts:72-79 checks only __host and __hostSync. Not exploitable as far as read: the invocation id is random (vm.ts:209).
problems.fix: Wrap PRELUDE in an IIFE returning only what __invoke and __shape need. Extend the escape test to these names.

problems.title: A VM can be disposed under an in-flight call
problems.evidence: compile.ts:79-85 retain() calls dispose() directly. invoke defers dispose until bridges are idle (vm.ts:236-237), but dispose() tears the VM down (vm.ts:241-253). Not run.
problems.fix: In retain, mark the VM broken instead; invoke's finally disposes it when idle.

problems.title: Section keys can collide
problems.evidence: compile.ts:217 uses name-id unless id equals name. Extension a with section b-c and extension a-b with section c both give a-b-c. An extension named files with section files gets key files, the same as the built-in section at prompt.ts:76. Effect in pi-durable on a duplicate key: UNVERIFIED.
problems.fix: Always use name:id and drop the special case.

problems.title: A timed-out call keeps running its bridge work
problems.evidence: vm.ts:217-220 rejects the caller after 30 s, but the script's pending bridge call (for example a write-effect yuki.call) keeps running. The model sees a failure and may retry.
problems.fix: Document yuki.env.callId as the idempotency key for external tools (compile.ts:204 already sends it), or stop starting new bridge work after invoke gives up.

problems.title: Install can report an error after the extension is installed
problems.evidence: extensions.ts:265 awaits scheduleTriggers after the proposal is deleted. A throw from cancelBy returns ok:false while the row exists, and the 'extension' event is never sent (extensions.ts:269).
problems.fix: Send the installed event before scheduling triggers, or catch the trigger error and record it with setError.

overengineering.title: names() on UserExtensions has no caller
apps/server/measure-worker
overengineering.evidence: entry.ts (116 lines), quickjs-probe.ts (17), wrangler.jsonc (12). No script or doc refers to it.
overengineering.why: An experiment with no caller. Delete after confirming the measured numbers are recorded in architecture.md.

overengineering.title: check.ts re-implements the bridge
overengineering.evidence: check.ts:74-111 repeats compile.ts toolBridge (compile.ts:149-185). Its egress test (check.ts:93) skips hostAllowed's lowercasing (manifest.ts:94-97).
overengineering.why: Compile with fake ScriptPorts and run the real bridge. That removes a copy that already differs.

overengineering.title: Arguments validated twice for yuki.call
overengineering.why: Small. Keep the second check, since hooks may change arguments.

overengineering.title: Global slot for the wasm module
overengineering.why: Pass the module through BuildAgentInput.scripts. Not urgent.

overengineering.title: Skills vs extension sections (overlap)
overengineering.evidence: A skill is lazy instruction text. A text-only extension section is always-on instruction text (compile.ts:216-220). The catalog is a list of reviewed bundles.
overengineering.why: They differ in when they cost context. Do not add a third instruction mechanism.

overengineering.title: Talker and worker tool split
overengineering.why: Keeps the lead's tool list small; it is the design the work tool describes.

overengineering.title: Bridge limits: continue cap, memory retire, wall clock, step budget
overengineering.why: Each has a tested failure it prevents (script-vm.test.ts:58-70, 124-138).

tests: Covered: script-vm.test.ts (11: run, bridge, refused call, step limit, memory retire, escape check, imports, syntax error, outliving a call, overlapping calls). user-extensions.test.ts (17: state and call, sections, read GET only, calls refused, hooks, wraps, name clash, onYield limit, mutual calls, catalog freshness, extension_check). extension-store.test.ts (7: install, secrets per host, egress, switches, state scopes, uninstall, users apart). skills.test.ts (6). agent-factory.test.ts (6). core/protocol/test/extensions.test.ts (2). CLI: apps/cli/src/verify/suites/extensions*.ts and composio-extension.ts. Gaps: no test that a read tool cannot state.set; no test that extension_check rejects a trigger install would refuse; the escape test checks only __host and __hostSync; no test of an update during an in-flight call; no test of section key collisions. Not run: the server test suite. Two probes ran in /tmp/audit/probe (prelude visibility, rrule acceptance), both confirmed. The other findings come from reading the code.
